requirement: Under {cite}`requirements.cli.skill_structure`, the `habeas-requirements` skill MUST be the home of drafting, reviewing, and agreeing requirements, the requirement review criteria, the procedure for choosing references, and the criteria the assessment applies to code and tests.
rationale:
structural: The only structural obligation in `requirements.cli.skill_structure.requirements` is a placement one. The `habeas-requirements` skill MUST be the home of four topics: drafting, reviewing and agreeing requirements; the requirement review criteria; the procedure for choosing references; and the criteria the assessment applies to code and tests. An alternative that kept the same behavior but put these topics in another skill, or split them across skills, would violate the clause. The clause is therefore not discretionary.

Both supplied roots carry the implementation edge. They are `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md` and `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/references/review-prompt.md`, and together they make up the skill.

The prose in the node reads was elided, so I judged coverage from the section structure:
- Drafting, reviewing and agreeing requirements: `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md` has `section[Habeas requirements]/section[Workflow]` and `section[Writing chapters]`.
- Requirement review criteria: `SKILL.md` has `section[What the review checks]`, and `references/review-prompt.md` has `section[Requirement group review]/section[Criteria]`.
- Procedure for choosing references: `SKILL.md` has `section[Choosing references]`.
- Criteria applied to code and tests: `references/review-prompt.md` has `section[Requirement group review]` with `section[Finding gaps]`, `section[Criteria]` and `section[Report]`.

No further implementation root is needed, because the skill's own files are the roots. I did not check the sibling skills for duplicated statements of these topics. That belongs to the parent requirement `requirements.cli.skill_structure`, not this one.

behavioral: The requirement says the `habeas-requirements` skill is the home of five topics. They are drafting, reviewing and agreeing requirements, the requirement review criteria, the procedure for choosing references, and the criteria the assessment applies to code and tests. Each topic is stated in full in exactly one skill, and that skill is its home. The one marked test is `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_requirements_skill_is_home_of_drafting_review_references_and_criteria]`. It covers each obligation:

- **Drafting, reviewing, agreeing.** The test looks for "Draft. Write drafts", "Review. Sort the new and changed requirements" and "**Gate:**" in the numbered steps of `habeas-requirements`' Workflow section, using `workflow_steps`.
- **Choosing references.** It asserts that the `## Choosing references` section of `SKILL.md` exists and contains "A *root* is".
- **Criteria applied to code and tests.** It asserts that the `## What the review checks` section contains the untested-obligation criterion and the supervising-agent statement.
- **Requirement review criteria.** It asserts that the `## Criteria` section of `references/review-prompt.md` contains "**Compound:**", "**Checkable:**" and "**One reading:**". That file is a reference file of this skill, so it counts as part of the skill.
- **Exactly one home.** `assert_home("habeas-requirements")` asserts that the skill (`SKILL.md` plus its references) contains every `home_markers` phrase for it. Those phrases include the Gate, the root definition, the review-checks heading, the group-review prompt heading and "**Compound:**". It also asserts that none of the other four skills contains any of those phrases. A skill that restated one of these topics verbatim would fail the test.

The `section`, `workflow_steps`, `assert_text`, `skill_files` and `bundled_skill` helpers really extract and check the bundled skill text. No assertion is vacuous. A skill that moved or dropped a topic, or duplicated a marker phrase elsewhere, would fail.

The "in full" and "exactly one" obligations can only be checked through marker phrases, because the skill text is prose. That is the reasonable way to test them, so I report no behavioral gap.

text: Under {cite}`requirements.cli.skill_structure`, the `habeas-requirements` skill MUST be the home of drafting, reviewing, and agreeing requirements, the requirement review criteria, the procedure for choosing references, and the criteria the assessment applies to code and tests.

Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST jointly give the direction that the requirements on them specify. A skill consists of its `SKILL.md` and the files under its `references/` directory. Each topic MUST be stated in full in exactly one skill, its home.
